title: Chitosan- and alginate-based biopolymeric composites for the adsorption of heavy metal ions from wastewater: modification strategies, composite architectures, adsorption behaviour and regeneration
content: Chitosan and alginate offer complementary amino, hydroxyl and carboxylate functionality for the removal of dissolved metal contaminants. Their practical performance depends on chemical modification, network stability, solution composition and sorbent architecture. This narrative review examines modification strategies, composite architectures, adsorption behaviour and regeneration, with particular attention to chitosan–alginate hybrids. The review links polymer chemistry and fabrication to reported adsorption performance, distinguishing literature-reported capacities from evidence of mechanism and operational durability. A descriptive compilation identifies study-specific results and gaps in experimental reporting. It is not a normalised benchmark or a systematic meta-analysis. Hybridisation and functionalisation can improve selected properties, but the available cross-study data do not establish universal superiority over single-polymer sorbents or isolate donor chemistry from composition and test conditions. Langmuir and pseudo-second-order fits describe equilibrium and kinetic data without independently proving chemisorption or rate control. Within-study controls, explicit aqueous speciation, distinct desorption and capacity-retention metrics, and validation under competitive continuous-flow conditions are needed for defensible comparison and scale-up.
